what: Near the bottom of the panel (around 45% of its height), terrain built from noise ridges is stamped as half-filled square dots on a 5px grid, with overlapping blobs laid beneath as filled areas. Dot noise and area noise drift in different directions at .05 per second, so the terrain keeps changing slowly. Black panel: pale gray dots. White panel: ink dots and pale gray areas. Red panel: darker red areas and dots (skin variable). WebGL shader

options.height: Ground height (share of board height), default .45
options.speed: Flow speed, default .05 — 0 means still ground
options.dots: Share where the dot lands (0~1), default .55
options.fill: Share of the painted area (0~1), default .38
options.--fx-dot · --fx-fill: Dot color and face color, default 22% and 8% of the text color. When the panel color changes, send the element an fx:paint event so it reads again

note: The original draws the ground as a letter (ASCII) panel and merges it inside the tear shader between blocks. The part draws only the ground separately — to blend in the tear with one shader, put the same noise into that shader, as the site side (index.js stage) does

from.where: lookbook.html·error.html·work.html bottom ground, index.js stage shader (black·white·red block ground) — original mask-scroll.js ASCII ground·pixelate.js
